blog_posts.title: Industrial cleaning trials: scope, isolate, contain, release
blog_posts.body:
## Treat the trial as maintenance work

An industrial cleaning trial starts with the asset and work controls, not a product promise. Record the equipment, soil or deposit, materials, current chemical, operating window, people who can authorize the work, and the acceptance endpoint before choosing chemistry.

## The four-gate plan

1. **Scope.** Review the exact SKU's current SDS and label against the task, concentration, substrate, ventilation, and site chemical-approval process.
2. **Isolate.** Where cleaning exposes workers to unexpected energization or stored energy, the site's hazardous-energy procedure and authorized personnel control the isolation.
3. **Contain.** Decide where rinse water, removed solids, oil, and spent solution will go before opening the container. Stormwater, sewer, waste, and permit decisions remain site- and jurisdiction-specific.
4. **Release.** Name the person who accepts the result and the recorded endpoint for rinsing, inspection, testing, reassembly, and return to service.

## Evidence boundary

A product document does not replace the site work plan, permit, lockout procedure, wastewater decision, or competent-person approval. This article is a planning framework, not legal, safety, environmental, or engineering approval.

## Primary sources

- [OSHA Hazard Communication, 29 CFR 1910.1200](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.1200)
- [OSHA Control of Hazardous Energy, 29 CFR 1910.147](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.147)
- [EPA industrial stormwater fact sheets](https://www.epa.gov/npdes/industrial-stormwater-fact-sheet-series)

Send the current chemical, task, asset, material, wastewater route, and reopening criteria through the [chemical-mapping intake](/contact?type=audit).

blog_posts.title: Food-plant cleaning: keep CIP, sanitation, and release separate
blog_posts.body:
## First decide whether the method is CIP

The FDA Food Code describes clean-in-place equipment as equipment cleaned by circulating or flowing detergent, rinse water, and sanitizing solution through fixed piping and equipment surfaces. Manual in-place cleaning is not automatically CIP. Map the circuit, flow path, temperature, concentration, contact time, drain points, and rinse endpoint before naming the method.

## Cleaning and sanitation answer different questions

Cleaning removes soil from the defined equipment and surface. The food-safety plan still controls allergen cross-contact, contamination prevention, sanitizing or disinfection, chemical suitability, and records. A cleaning observation cannot establish a microbiological, allergen, or food-contact release.

## Define release before the trial

The customer should select the acceptance method for the hazard and process: documented visual inspection, rinse endpoint, residue check, ATP, allergen, microbiological, or another validated method as applicable. Record limitations and failed criteria as well as the accepted result.

## Evidence boundary

Cleaning evidence is not sanitation or disinfection evidence. An antimicrobial or disinfectant claim requires the exact EPA-registered product used according to its label; one product cannot borrow another product's registration. Product selection remains subject to current exact-SKU documents, material review, the food-safety plan, and site approval.

## Primary sources

- [FDA Food Code 2022](https://www.fda.gov/media/184685/download)
- [21 CFR 117.35, Sanitary operations](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-117/subpart-B/section-117.35)
- [EPA selected registered disinfectants](https://www.epa.gov/pesticide-registration/selected-epa-registered-disinfectants)

Use the [food-and-beverage audit intake](/contact?type=audit&industry=Food%20%26%20Beverage) to provide the circuit, soil, current method, and release criteria.

blog_posts.excerpt: A source-led way to separate the CIP method, cleaning result, sanitation decision, and customer-defined release criteria.

blog_posts.title: Cooling-tower cleaning belongs inside the water-management plan
blog_posts.body:
## Start with the facility program

Cooling-tower cleaning is one controlled task inside a broader water-management program. The facility team owns system scope, responsible people, control locations, monitoring, corrective action, shutdown coordination, and return to service. A cleaner does not create a water-management program or establish that the facility meets its water-management obligations.

## Build the maintenance window around the system

Record tower duty and redundancy, system volume, metallurgy, deposits, prior treatment, monitoring points, isolation limits, aerosol controls, worker protection, containment, disposal route, and the operating endpoint needed for reopening. Use the current equipment requirements and facility procedure to set circulation, inspection, flushing, refill, and verification steps.

## Keep product and program evidence separate

Scale, corrosion, suspended solids, and microbiological growth are different control problems. Review each proposed product against its exact function and current records. Certification, performance, potable-water, antimicrobial, safety, and discharge statements require their own exact-product evidence and cannot be inferred from the water-management plan.

## Evidence boundary

Cleaning chemistry is one controlled task inside the facility program, not a substitute for risk management, monitoring, disinfection strategy, engineering review, or jurisdictional requirements. This article provides intake structure, not site approval.

## Primary sources

- [ASHRAE Standard 188 and Guideline 12 scopes](https://www.ashrae.org/technical-resources/standards-and-guidelines/titles-purposes-and-scopes)
- [CDC cooling-tower cleaning procedure](https://www.cdc.gov/infection-control/hcp/environmental-control/appendix-c-water.html)
- [DOE cooling-water efficiency opportunities for federal data centers](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/cooling-water-efficiency-opportunities-federal-data-centers)

Use the [water-treatment audit intake](/contact?type=audit&industry=HVAC%20%2F%20Water%20Treatment) to send system volume, metallurgy, current program, wastewater route, and reopening criteria.

blog_posts.body:
## The efficiency tax of scale

Even a thin scale layer drops heat-transfer efficiency and raises energy cost.

## A lower-hazard descale

VertKleen descaling chemistry targets carbonate and mineral scale while holding a lower HMIS profile than conventional acid blends.

> Ask for a dilution guide before your next CIP cycle.

blog_posts.title: What HMIS 0-0-0 Actually Means for Your Facility
blog_posts.body:
## The three numbers

HMIS rates **Health**, **Flammability**, and **Physical hazard** from 0 to 4. A `0-0-0` product scores the lowest on those three HMIS fields for that exact product and revision.

## What it does not decide

HMIS alone does not determine PPE, storage, transport classification, ventilation, training, material compatibility, or a site procedure. Review the exact SKU's current SDS, label, task, concentration, and workplace controls before approval.

See our [products](/products) and request the current product documents.
